title: DHCP Snooping: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Anyone can plug in a D H C P server. A rogue one hands out bad addresses, and sends your traffic to the attacker. D H C P snooping stops it.

lines.t: Anyone can run a DHCP server
A rogue hands out bad addresses

scenes.heading: The bouncer at the party
scenes.narration: At a VIP party, the bouncer lets trusted hosts through the main door, and that's your real D H C P server. Everyone else uses side doors, and they're untrusted. If an untrusted guest tries to hand out party passes, the bouncer stops them. That means dropping offers and acknowledgements on untrusted ports. The bouncer also keeps a list of who got which address, called the binding database.

scenes.heading: Setting it up
scenes.narration: Turn it on globally. Turn it on per V L A N. And trust only the port that faces the real server.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. Snooping doesn't block all D H C P on untrusted ports. It blocks only the server messages. It's turned on globally and per V L A N, not interface by interface. And the database stores client addresses, not the server's.

items.wrong: Blocks all DHCP on untrusted ports

items.right: Global and per VLAN; trust is per interface
It stores client IP, MAC, VLAN, port

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva DHCP snooping lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. D H C P snooping blocks rogue D H C P servers. Only trust the port facing your real server. The binding database powers other protections too. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva DHCP snooping lab.

points.t: Trust only the real server's port
The binding database helps other features
